docs.title: India’s $13.62 billion food ingredients opportunity: 2 stocks, two very different bets
docs.text: According to Grand View Research, the speciality food ingredients market in India was valued at US$8.32 billion in 2025 and is expected to reach US$13.62 billion by 2033, with a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 6.2%. Today, the market is led by sensory ingredients, with functional ingredients expected to grow at a faster pace. This creates an opportunity for suppliers of ingredients that help to maintain food quality, improve texture and extend shelf life. Gujarat Ambuja Exports and Camlin Fine Sciences offer alternative routes to this opportunity through maize-derived ingredients, fermentation products, antioxidants and specialised food formulations. Take a deeper look at their expansion plans, commercial execution and valuations. Gujarat Ambuja Exports: Turning Maize Into a Higher-Value Ingredient Business Gujarat Ambuja Exports Limited (GAEL) is an agro-processing company with businesses spanning maize processing, starch derivatives, sweeteners, edible oils and other products. Its relevance to the speciality food ingredients theme comes from ingredients such as maltodextrin, dextrose, sorbitol, liquid glucose and starch derivatives, which serve food processing, dairy and nutrition applications, alongside pharmaceutical and industrial markets. FE Stock Insights on WhatsApPGet instant alerts on high-conviction investment themes and fundamental deep dives—direct from Financial Express.Join now The investment question is whether its expanding processing and fermentation capabilities can increase the contribution of value-added products rather than merely expand production capacity. Hubli: Capacity Bet on Long-Dated On 9 September 2026, GAEL announced its proposal to establish an 850-tonnes-per-day (TPD) corn wet-milling plant at Hubli, Karnataka, subject to regulatory approvals and clearances. The proposed investment of ₹333 crore will be funded through internal accruals, with commissioning expected by the fourth quarter of the financial year 2028-29 (Q4 FY29). The proposed facility is designed to produce 400 TPD of corn starch, 150 TPD of sweeteners and 300 TPD of feed ingredients. Once completed, Hubli's total manufacturing capacity is expected to reach 1,600 TPD, comprising 700 TPD of corn starch, 400 TPD of sweeteners and derivatives, and 500 TPD of feed ingredients. GAEL also plans to raise its overall corn wet-milling capacity from 5,600 TPD to 9,000 TPD by 2030. This is a longer-term target, distinct from the capacity currently installed and operational. The feed ingredient component also means that the entire planned increase cannot be treated as an expansion of speciality food ingredients. From Maltodextrin to Fermentation: The Value-Addition Strategy GAEL's Q1 FY27 investor presentation records several capacity additions completed during FY26. At Hubli, the company commissioned a 30,000-tonnes-per-annum (TPA) sodium gluconate fermentation facility. It also increased maltodextrin capacity from 7,000 TPA to 23,000 TPA. At Sitarganj, maize-processing capacity rose from 1,200 TPD to 1,950 TPD. These developments widen GAEL's ability to supply ingredients for food processing, nutrition and dairy applications. However, sodium gluconate also serves pharmaceutical, construction and other industrial markets. Its entire capacity or potential revenue should therefore not be attributed to food ingredients. The company has also set a target to increase the combined installed capacity of its fermentation-based products to 1,20,000 TPA by 2028, up from 30,000 TPA at the initial sodium gluconate facility. This represents a fourfold increase relative to the stated initial capacity, not a forecast of fourfold revenue or profit growth. The outcome will depend on the products covered by the target, commissioning schedules, utilisation, pricing and demand. Himmatnagar and Hubli: Two Projects, Two Timelines GAEL is pursuing a separate 900-TPD greenfield corn wet-milling project at Himmatnagar, Gujarat, targeted for FY27 in its investor presentation. This is distinct from the 850-TPD Hubli project, for which commissioning is expected by Q4 FY29. The disclosed project details establish the planned capacity and timelines, but do not provide a complete project-wise account of capital expenditure or a quantified earnings contribution. GAEL reported capital investment of ₹259.52 crore in FY26 versus ₹281.40 crore in FY25. In its Q1 FY27 investor presentation, it said its cumulative investment during FY22-FY26 was ₹1,243 crore, funded through internal accruals. Debt, Cash Flow and the Ability to Fund Growth In its Q1 FY27 investor presentation, GAEL describes its balance sheet as near debt-free and reports total borrowings of ₹434 crore. It also shows an operating cash flow of ₹543 crore in its five-year financial overview, apart from the ₹1,243 crore that has been invested in FY22-FY26. The borrowings, operating cash flow and historical capital expenditure provide context for assessing GAEL's funding capacity. Q1 FY27: What the Numbers Reveal and Conceal GAEL reported consolidated revenue from operations of ₹1,466.51 crore in Q1 FY27, an increase of 13.57% year-on-year (YoY) and a decline of 8.01% quarter-on-quarter (QoQ). Consolidated profit after tax (PAT) rose to ₹135.32 crore from ₹65.02 crore in Q1 FY26, but declined from ₹176.77 crore in Q4 FY26. Its Maize Processing division reported revenue of ₹1,084.75 crore in Q1 FY27. Revenue was flat YoY but rose by 36.3% QoQ. This division includes both maize processing and value-added products, so it is not a direct measure of speciality food ingredients sales. The figures offer a broad view of GAEL's operating performance, but they do not reveal whether the higher maltodextrin capacity has translated into stronger food-specific revenue, improved margins or better utilisation. The company does not separately disclose quarterly revenue or profit for speciality food ingredients in the information considered here. Distribution Reach Versus Product-Level Dem

Shares of Vishal Mega Mart remained under pressure during Thursday’s trading session. The diversified retail stock has declined nearly 30% over the last six months. While the brokerage reduced its target price for the stock after Q2FY27 results announcement, it continued to remain bullish on the stock because of its diversified category mix and business model.
Vishal Mega Mart share price outlook

We believe Blinkit is capitalizing on the QCom opportunity via aggressive network rollout and larger scale feeding into better unit economics. Eternal announced dark.ai, a privacy-first AI assistant aimed at power users, running on frontier open-weight models on Eternal's own infrastructure – pending details on monetization and cost structure, we have a neutral stance. docs.title: Buy Hindalco Ltd for the Target Rs 1,170 by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
Multiple growth levers to drive earnings inflection and deleveraging 
We maintain our positive stance on Hindalco Industries (HNDL), as the recent correction, driven by declining LME prices and supply normalization, appears largely priced in, while the long-term growth outlook remains intact. This correction offers an attractive risk-reward opportunity in a diversified play spanning India’s integrated aluminum business with a premium value-added product portfolio, global aluminum recycling through Novelis, and the domestic copper growth opportunity. HNDL offers strong earnings growth visibility, driven by aggressive capacity expansion, downstream integration, structural cost savings, and Novelis’ operational recovery, positioning the company for a structural earnings inflection and B/S deleveraging. Net debt/EBITDA is expected to decline to below ~1.5x from 1.95x in 1QFY27, with execution and Novelis’ recovery remaining the key monitorables. Currently, the stock trades at 5.4x EV/EBITDA and 1.3x P/B on FY28 estimates. We reiterate our BUY rating on HNDL with an SOTP-based TP of INR1,170 on FY28E.
 Aggressive upstream expansion provides long-term growth visibility 
* HNDL India has outlined a capex plan of INR450-500b to expand its aluminum and copper capacities, strengthen resource security, and increase value-added offerings.
* Aluminum capacity is expected to rise from 1,340ktpa to 1,714ktpa (+28%), while copper capacity will increase from 421ktpa to 721ktpa (+71%).
* HNDL targets doubling its capacity to over 2,000ktpa for aluminum, +5,500ktpa for alumina, and 1,200ktpa for copper, providing long-term growth visibility
 Cost optimization via backward integration and RE share 
* HNDL is reducing external coal dependence through captive mining, with existing Gare Palma IV/4 & 5 and Kathautia mines meeting only 2-3% of its coal requirements.
* We believe the development of Chakla, Bandha, and Meenakshi mines is expected to improve energy security and deliver ~USD200/t savings over FY24 cost levels.
* Meanwhile, renewable capacity of 470MW is expected to increase to ~884MW by FY27 and 1.5GW by FY28, supporting the company's target of sourcing 30% of its energy from renewables by 2030.
* Novelis' recovery is gaining traction following the restart of the Oswego hot mill in Jun’26, with operational normalization and insurance proceeds supporting cash flow recovery (expects positive free cash flow in 4QFY27).
* The 600ktpa Bay Minette facility, equivalent to ~16% of US capacity including recycling, will drive incremental growth and diversify Novelis' footprint, reducing its dependence on Oswego (accounts for ~40% of US domestic automotive supply).
* Gradual operational recovery and Bay Minette's ramp-up should support earnings growth and cash generation, although production normalization, insurance recoveries, and elevated leverage remain key monitorables.
* HNDL’s India operations are net debt-free, while consolidated net debt-toEBITDA ratio stood at 1.95x as of Jun’26. The announced/ongoing expansion is set to position HNDL as the global leader, though any delay in the stated timeline and cost escalations could pressure cash flows.
* The stock is trading at 5.4x FY28E EV/EBITDA and 1.3x FY28E P/B. We reiterate our BUY rating on HNDL with our SOTP-based TP of INR1,170.

docs.text:
Supported by broad-based disbursement growth, benign asset quality, and contained credit cost, MMFS reported a healthy 2QFY27. PAT was up 55% yoy to Rs8.82bn and AUM rose ~15% yoy to Rs1.47trn, aided by strong momentum in the non-wheels segment. GS2+GS3 fell to a multiyear low of 8.1%, with the usual seasonal deterioration in 2Q largely absent. Management sees existing overlays of Rs8.52bn as an adequate cushion against external stress, and currently sees no need to build more. However, it flagged near-term headwinds: rising COF amid rate hikes, draft insurance-commission norms that could dent fee income, drought-related collection risk, and softer early festive demand, particularly in tractors. Margins remain at the lower end of the level needed for target ROA, though the drag from excess liquidity and trade advances should ease. Management retained its medium-term guidance on growth, credit cost, and ROA, and said the MRHFL merger is on track. Factoring in these near-term headwinds, we cut our FY27-29 estimates, resulting in a 1-2% cut in our FY27- 29E EPS. We maintain BUY while lowering our Sep-27E TP by ~10% to Rs370 (Rs410 earlier), implying FY28E PBV of 1.7x.
MMFS delivered a good 2QFY27, with PAT up 55% yoy to Rs8.82bn, driven by contained credit cost of 1.6% (vs 2.2% in 2QFY26 and 1.5% in 1QFY27) and moderating opex. Margins were flat yoy at 7.0% but contracted by ~30bps qoq due to excess liquidity and seasonal trade advances, which management expects to normalize. Higher fee income and stable COF partly offset the decline, keeping 1H margin at 7.1%, in line with guidance. Asset quality continues to improve, with GS2+GS3 at 8.1% and PCR at 56.6%.
 Steady outlook, but COF, insurance, and drought risks linger 
Management retained its medium-term targets of 16–18% AUM growth, GS2+GS3 of <10%, 1.3–1.7% credit cost, and 2.2–2.5% ROA. Wheels should grow slightly ahead of the industry, with SME, PL, and mortgages driving alpha, though the high 2H base could weigh on disbursements. Margins face COF pressure, as ~48% of borrowings are floating (mostly repo/T-bill-linked) and ~Rs270bn matures over the next six months, while the largely fixed-rate wheels book reprices via new loans. Pricing on new loans, faster nonwheels repricing, fee levers, and an easing liquidity/trade-advance drag should partly offset this, keeping NIM near the ~7% needed for target ROA. Draft insurancecommission norms remain a risk to fees. With 1H stress already contained, the usual 2H seasonal improvement is likely to be muted, limiting further credit-cost gains, and the drought's impact on tractor collections will be clearer once half-yearly installments fall due. Mortgages may initially dilute ROA, but the MRHFL merger should remove duplication and simplify distribution.
 Adjust estimates; maintain BUY with a revised TP of Rs370 
Factoring in the 2QFY27 performance and near-term headwinds from rising COF, insurance-commission norms, and drought-related risks, we cut our FY27–29E EPS by 1–2% (Exhibit 2). We maintain BUY but lower our Sep-27E TP to Rs370 (from Rs410), implying 1.7x FY28E PBV

* FD growth to remain the priority, with margins range-bound: Eternal has reiterated its long-term target of 20%+ annual NOV growth, supported by customer additions and high ordering frequency, despite high competitive intensity. Margins are expected to remain broadly flat in the next 1-2 years as incremental profitability is reinvested to expand the market and drive absolute EBITDA growth. For FY27/FY28, we build in ~20% YoY NOV growth and 5.6%/6.0% adj. EBITDA margin as % of NOV.
* Blinkit’s expansion to accelerate, with NOV growth expected to pick up: NOV grew 79.3% YoY in 2Q, and growth is expected to pick up from 3Q as new stores come online and ramp up. Despite intense competition, Blinkit’s assortment intelligence, category breadth and execution capabilities are supporting customer acquisition and store paybacks.
* The FY27-end store target has been raised to 3,500 from 3,000 earlier, with a further increase to ~5,000 by FY28-end. Improving store paybacks in smaller cities and a more predictable competitive environment were cited as key factors supporting the acceleration. Blinkit remains ahead of its 60% NOV CAGR guidance over the three-year period and we model 86%/74% YoY NOV growth for FY27/FY28.
* Mature-city profitability to support incremental store expansion in QC: Management indicated that mature cities already generate adjusted EBITDA margins of over 5%, while cities accounting for ~70% of NOV are adjusted EBITDA positive and those representing ~96% of NOV are contribution positive. While new stores weigh on margins during the initial ramp-up, it expects profitability improvements in mature stores and cities to more than offset this impact.
* District and Hyperpure progress toward profitability: District is on track to achieve adjusted EBITDA breakeven within 4-6 quarters from Jan’26 and deliver INR280b in NOV and INR14b in adj. EBITDA by FY30. Hyperpure revenue grew 22.7% YoY, with restaurant count rising to 85,000 from 62,000; adj. EBITDA margin improved to 0.9% from -0.5% a year ago.
* Dark.ai represents an early-stage investment in privacy-focused AI: Dark.ai is being developed as an AI application using fine-tuned open-weight models hosted on Eternal’s own infrastructure, with end-to-end encryption and usercontrolled encrypted memory. The product targets power users, including founders, researchers and enterprises, who require privacy for sensitive conversations and work. This was described as an early-stage opportunity, with monetization and investment requirements to be assessed following the launch.
* Agentic commerce – fulfilment infrastructure to determine the extent of disintermediation: As discussed in our earlier note (dated 14th Oct’26: Consumer AI agents: Our views on Instinct and Muse), we believe the impact of agentic commerce will vary by business model, with platforms controlling fulfilment and supply-chain infrastructure better positioned than pure intermediaries. Management expects Zomato and Blinkit to remain relatively resilient given their integrated delivery and inventory networks, while District faces higher exposure as its underlying supply can be accessed independently of the platform. It also expects in-app AI interfaces to address repeat-order use cases, while browsing-led discovery remains important for food delivery.
* Eternal's FD business is stable, while Blinkit continues to offer a long runway to participate in the structural shift in retail, grocery, and e-commerce. We trim our FY27 EPS estimate, driven by a substantially higher tax rate in 2Q, as all tax shields at the standalone parent level have been exhausted in carried forward losses in FY27 and standalone entity profits will now be taxed at the full rate. While competitive intensity remains elevated, competition is becoming more predictable, and the business model appears established, with a clear path to structurally higher margins.
* We continue to factor in management's long-term growth trajectory of 60%+ NOV growth for the QC business, along with gradual margin expansion through store maturity and operating leverage. We expect Eternal to report PAT margins of 0.8%/1.4% in FY27/28. Our TP of INR420 implies a 35% upside from the current price. We reiterate our BUY rating.

docs.title: Buy Vishal Mega Mart Ltd for the Target Rs 125 by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
Festive shift affects 2Q growth and profitability 
* Vishal Mega Mart (VMM) delivered a slightly weaker 2QFY27, with revenue rising ~14% YoY (vs. our est. of ~16% YoY), led by 5.4% SSSG (a 300-400bp dent due to the festive shift) and ~10.5% YoY area addition.
* Pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin contracted ~90bp YoY to 7.2%, due to a weaker gross margin (-30bp YoY, ~20bp impact due to the festive shift) and higher employee costs (minimum wage hikes and ESOP costs). Pre-Ind AS EBITDA and PAT inched up ~1%/4% YoY, missing our estimates by 5%.
* Festive demand started strongly in 3Q, with no moderation in demand. VMM reiterated its target of ~10% SSSG for FY27. Growth was led by market share gains, with no further price hikes planned at current levels.
* Gross margin is expected to remain stable in 2H as cost reengineering is likely to offset RM inflationary pressures. Operating leverage should help deliver ~30bp annual EBITDA margin expansion over the medium term.
* VMM’s operating performance remains robust, led by its differentiated product mix, strong own-brand portfolio, and best-in-class cost controls. However, concerns on promoter stake sales and long-term ownership (postPE exit) remain key overhangs.
* We cut our FY27-29 EBITDA and PAT estimates by ~2-4% due to higher employee expenses and a slight moderation in our SSSG estimate.
* We model a CAGR of 18%/24%/26% in revenue/pre-IND AS EBITDA/PAT over FY26-29E, driven by ~10% CAGR in area, double-digit SSSG and ~45bp of annual pre-IND AS EBITDA margin expansion.
* We reiterate our BUY rating on the stock with a revised TP of INR125, premised on a DCF-implied valuation of ~24x Dec’28E pre-IND AS 116 EV/EBITDA (implying ~38x Dec’28E EPS).
 Resilient revenue growth and margins in 1HFY27 despite the festive shift 
* Consolidated revenue at INR71.3b grew ~16% YoY, driven by ~7.7% adj. SSSG (~9.5% adjusted for the festive shift) and ~10.5% store area additions.
* Gross profit at INR20.2b grew ~16% YoY as GM remained stable YoY at 28.3%.
* Reported EBITDA at INR9.6b was up ~12% YoY as the margin contracted ~50bp YoY to 13.4%, due to festive shift and higher minimum wages.
* Pre-IND AS 116 EBITDA (post-ESOP charges) grew ~13% YoY to INR6.2b, with the EBITDA margin contracting ~30bp YoY to 8.7%.
* Reported PAT at INR4.2b rose ~16% YoY, driven by EBITDA growth and higher other income (up 92% YoY).
* For 2HFY27, the required growth rates for revenue/pre-IND AS EBITDA/PAT growth are 21%/21%/23%.
* VMM remains among the most consistent retailers within our coverage. We believe its diversified category mix, ownership of opening-price-point products, significant contribution from its own brands, and lean cost structure provide it with a strong moat against intense competition from both offline and online value retailers.
* However, concerns over potential promoter stake sales and LT promoter ownership (post the private equity’s exit), remain key overhangs for the stock.
* We cut our FY27-29 EBITDA and PAT estimates by ~2-4% due to higher employee expenses and slight moderation in SSSG estimate.
* We model a CAGR of 18%/24%/26% in revenue/pre-IND AS EBITDA/PAT over FY26-29E, driven by ~10% CAGR in area, double-digit SSSG and ~45bp annual pre-IND AS EBITDA margin expansion.
* We reiterate our BUY rating on the stock with a revised TP of INR125 (earlier INR135), premised on a DCF-implied valuation of ~24x Dec’28E pre-IND AS 116 EV/EBITDA (implying ~38x Dec’28E EPS).

docs.title: Buy Indian Hotels Ltd for the Target Rs 870 by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
MICE, BRICS, and marquee hotel renovations drive growth 
* Indian Hotels (IH) reported healthy consolidated revenue growth of 22% YoY in 2QFY27, led by 26% growth in the standalone business and 17% growth in subsidiaries. Growth in the standalone business was led by room revenue (RevPAR up 28% YoY, led by ARR/OR growth of 19%/700bp), followed by F&B revenue (up 20%), other services (up 49%), and management fees (up 16%).
* IH has upgraded its FY27 revenue guidance to 15-17% (from 12-14% growth), driven by sustained domestic travel demand, robust growth across its asset-light management business, and emerging brands such as Ginger, Qmin, amã Stays & Trails, and Tree of Life. Moreover, the company has a pipeline of 34,800 keys (with 81% of the signed pipeline being assetlight), almost equal to its current operational keys of 34,213, thereby supporting sustained growth momentum.
* We expect IH’s performance to continue its uptrend, with a CAGR of 14%/15%/19% in revenue/EBITDA/adj. PAT over FY26-28. We broadly maintain our FY27/FY28 EBITDA estimates and reiterate BUY with our SoTP-based TP of INR870.
 Domestic operating performance offsets softness in the international business 
* Revenue grew 22% YoY to INR24.8b (est. INR23.7b). Hotel segment grew 26%, while TajSATS declined 2% YoY to INR2.8b.
* EBITDA grew 24% YoY to INR7.1b (est. INR6.7b). EBITDA margin expanded 50bp YoY to 28.4%. Adj. PAT grew 24% YoY to INR3.5b (est. INR3.7b).
* Standalone revenue/EBITDA grew 26%/40% YoY to INR13.4b/INR5.2b, aided by an increase in RevPAR (up 28% YoY to INR13,860), led by ARR growth of 19% to INR16,902, with OR expanding 700bp to 82%. F&B/other services/management fee income grew 20%/49%/16% YoY.
* Subsidiary (consol less standalone) sales stood at INR11.5b, up 17% YoY. Subsidiary EBITDA came in at INR1.9b, down 7% YoY.
* UOH/St. James’ revenue grew 16%/14% YoY, with EBITDA for UOH declining 75% YoY, while St. James witnessed an EBITDA growth of 10%.
* For 1HFY27, Revenue/EBITDA/Adj. PAT grew 18%/20%/22% to INR48b/INR14b/INR7b.
* Gross debt stood at INR1.2b vs INR513m as of Mar’26. CFO stood at INR9.7b vs INR25b as of Mar’26. The company reported a gross cash of INR43.7b.
 Highlights from the management commentary 
* Domestic performance: Domestic hotel RevPAR growth of 28% was driven by resilient domestic demand, supported by large MICE events such as the BRICS Summit and renovations at marquee hotels, including Taj Palace New Delhi, President Mumbai, Taj West End Bengaluru, Taj Fort Aguada Goa, and Taj Lake Palace Udaipur.
* Ginger: The brand crossed 100 operational hotels, becoming India's first hotel brand to achieve this milestone, and is targeting 150 hotels by Mar’27. IH is integrating properties acquired through the ANK Pride transaction into Ginger, with nearly 75 signings completed and 30 properties already operating under the Ginger brand.
* Oriental Hotels merger: IH announced the merger of Oriental Hotels (OHL) with an appointed date of 1st Apr’27. The all-stock transaction has a share exchange ratio of 25 IH shares for every 117 OHL shares and is expected to increase IH's standalone operating revenue by 6–7% in FY28. The merger is expected to unlock operational synergies.
* International business: IH expects its international portfolio to improve in H2FY27, supported by the completion of renovation work at key properties and a gradual recovery in demand. London recorded double-digit revenue growth in October, following the completion of upgrades to meeting rooms, the lobby, and food and beverage facilities. However, margins were affected by higher fuel and power costs and the removal of a property tax waiver.
* We remain optimistic on IH’s growth outlook despite near-term geopolitical and macroeconomic uncertainties, led by healthy traction in the core business as well as new and reimagined businesses.
* We expect the strong momentum to continue in the medium term, led by:
1) a strong room addition pipeline in owned/management hotels (6,650/28,150 rooms)
3) continued favorable demand-supply dynamics

docs.title: Buy Yash Highvoltage Ltd For Target Rs.1,500 by Choice Institutional Equities
docs.text:
Strong Volume Growth and Improved Product Mix in H1FY27 
YASHHV reported strong H1FY27 performance, with revenue increasing 95% YoY to INR 1,945 Mn, supported by nearly 40% volume growth and a robust domestic demand. Improved product mix, higher realisation, cost-efficiencies and operating leverage supported margin expansion. The order book of INR 7,600 Mn and ramp-up of the Jarod greenfield facility support growth outlook.
 H1FY27 Growth Led by Strong Volumes and Higher Realisation 
* Revenue increased 95.3% YoY to INR 1.9 Bn, supported by 40% YoY volume growth (~4,000 bushings) and higher realisation, reflecting a strong domestic demand and a higher share of RIP bushings
* EBITDA rose 152.3% YoY to INR 0.5 Bn, with EBITDA margin expanding 620 bps YoY to 27.5%, driven by operating leverage, better product mix, higher price realisation and efficiency gains * PAT grew 165.7% YoY to INR 0.4 Bn, aided by higher operating profitability
 Margin Expansion Drivers and Localisation Benefits 
* Gross margin rose from 44.9% to 52%, attributed to product mix, nearly 40% higher volume, better realisation and cost-efficiency measures
* EBITDA margin expansion reflected customer pricing, stronger product mix, better vendor terms, factory efficiency and overhead leverage. Localisation of cores could lead to exclusion of import duty and freight expenses.
* Customer expectations and competitor pricing will determine how savings are passed on. Higher-voltage projects do not always earn higher margin, as profitability depends on project mix and factory utilisation
* Greenfield capex of INR 2,200 Mn: INR 1,060 Mn was deployed by 30 September, 2026, and the balance will be invested over the next 12 months. The brownfield OIP expansion at Halol is on track to complete in Q3FY27
* No major capex is planned beyond the current investment, which is sufficient to support revenue of INR 9,000–10,000 Mn by FY30–FY31. Only minor capex will be required to support volume growth

docs.title: Buy Aditya Birla Sun Life AMC Ltd for the Target Rs 1,160 by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
Core performance in line; other income drives a PAT beat 
* Aditya Birla Sun Life AMC (ABSLAMC)’s operating revenue grew 5% YoY/ 4% QoQ to ~INR4.8b (in-line). For 1HFY27, revenue grew 4% YoY. The yield for the quarter stood at 43.8bp vs. 43.4bp in 2QFY26 and 43.3bp in 1QFY27.
* Total opex grew 21% YoY to INR2.2b (in-line) reflecting a cost-to-income ratio of 44.6% vs. 38.7% in 2QFY26 (vs. our est. of 44.5%). EBITDA dipped 5% YoY to INR2.7b (in line), reflecting an EBITDA margin of 55.4% (vs. 61.3% in 2QFY26 and MOFSLe of 55.5%). EBITDA stood at INR5.3b in 1HFY27.
* The beat on other income resulted in a 15% beat on PAT, which stood at INR2.2b, declining 8% YoY and 29% QoQ. 1HFY27 PAT stood at INR5.3b. Core PAT for 2Q came in at INR1.9b (-8% YoY; in line).
* Employee expenses are likely to remain around 2QFY27 levels going forward. The newly launched ESOP scheme is expected to have an annual impact of INR140–150m, while earlier schemes could entail an annual impact of INR550–600m over the next two years.
* We have broadly kept our estimates intact considering the in-line operating performance in 2QFY27. We reiterate our BUY rating on the stock with a TP of INR1,160, based on a valuation of 38x FY28E core P/E.
 Key takeaways from the management commentary 
* Retention ratio has increased to ~25–30%, from just 4–5% driven by better performance and the redirection of investors to other schemes.
* EPFO mandates are cost-neutral, but can strengthen credibility and create opportunities for privately managed assets and overseas mandates.
* A dedicated team has been hired to build the SIF franchise, with a focus on driving product awareness and investor allocations.
* Improving flagship fund performance, stronger distribution traction, and an improving retention rate provide confidence in sustained AUM growth while disciplined cost management should support operating leverage. Continued improvement in flows and market share recovery remain key earnings drivers.
* The expanding alternatives, PMS, passive, SIF and GIFT City businesses provide meaningful long-term optionality beyond the core mutual fund franchise. As these businesses scale, they are expected to diversify revenue streams and support profitability, although execution and fundraising momentum remain the key monitorables.
* We have broadly kept our estimates intact considering the in-line operating performance in 2QFY27. We reiterate our BUY rating on the stock with a TP of INR1,160, based on a valuation of 38x FY28E core P/E.
